findings.title: A backup code plus any non-empty totpCode logs in without the password
findings.body: The password is only checked when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). Before this PR, sending a `totpCode` skipped the password check, but the TOTP branch still had to accept that code. Now the backup-code branch (line 131) comes first and replaces TOTP verification completely. So a POST to the credentials callback with `{email, password: "", totpCode: "x", backupCode: "<valid code>"}` skips the password at line 121, takes the backup-code branch, passes, and returns the user. NextAuth passes every request field into `authorize`. The result is that someone with a user's email and one leaked backup code gets a full session, with no password and no authenticator. Fix: reject requests that carry both `totpCode` and `backupCode`, or always verify the password on the backup-code path (for example, check `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`, or verify the password inside the backup-code branch).

findings.title: Backup codes are case-sensitive while the UI suggests uppercase
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, setup.ts:61). The login check only strips dashes before `indexOf` (here and in disable.ts:61). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX` (BackupCode.tsx:21), so a user who writes or types a code in uppercase gets `incorrect-backup-code` for a valid code, which is the one moment they have no other way in. Normalise with `.toLowerCase()` (and trim) before comparing, in both places.

findings.title: Two concurrent logins can both use the same backup code
findings.body: Consuming a code is a read (line 73), then an in-memory null (line 148), then an unconditional `prisma.user.update` (line 149). Two simultaneous requests with the same code both find it before either write lands, so both succeed, and the code is not really single-use. Consider a conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`, failing when the count is 0) or a transaction.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves the switch showing 2FA as off
findings.body: 2FA is now enabled on the server before the codes are shown, but `onEnable()` (which calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`, two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68) only runs from the Close button (line 269). If the user closes with Escape or a click outside, only `onOpenChange` runs (two-factor-auth.tsx:64). That just toggles `enableModalOpen`: the settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled, and `step` stays `DisplayBackupCodes`, so reopening the modal shows the old codes again. Call `onEnable()` (or invalidate) as soon as enable succeeds, or handle dismissal on this step the same way as Close.

findings.title: "Please generate them in your settings" points to a feature that does not exist
findings.body: Backup codes are only created by `totp/setup` (setup.ts:61-68), which refuses users who already have 2FA enabled (setup.ts:42-44). Users who enabled 2FA before this PR have `backupCodes = null`, and settings has no way to generate codes for them, short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA. The message sends them looking for an option that is not there. Reword it (e.g. "disable and re-enable two-factor authentication to generate backup codes") or add a regenerate action.

findings.title: The BackupCode component's function is named TwoFactor
findings.body: It is the default export, so imports work, but React DevTools and stack traces will show `TwoFactor` for this component, which is confusing next to the real `TwoFactor`. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

contracts.action: Log in with a backup code instead of TOTP
contracts.before_after: The TOTP path verifies the code against the secret. The password check before it is skipped whenever totpCode is non-empty (line 121), so the TOTP check was the only factor for those requests. The backup path takes priority over TOTP and never checks totpCode, so password+TOTP can both be bypassed by sending any totpCode.
contracts.visible_effect: On success signIn returns no error and login.tsx:155 redirects. Errors map to the incorrect_backup_code and missing_backup_codes messages (login.tsx:157-158).
contracts.failure_mode: Wrong-case codes are rejected (setup.ts:61 hex lowercase). A concurrent read-modify-write lets the same code be reused.

contracts.equivalent_path: Previous direct onEnable() call after successful enable
contracts.before_after: Before, onEnable closed the modal and invalidated viewer.me. Now that only happens from the Close button (line 266-270).
contracts.visible_effect: Dismissing via onOpenChange leaves the switch unchecked and the step stuck on DisplayBackupCodes.
contracts.failure_mode: The settings page shows 2FA as off until refetch/reload.

contracts.before_after: The password is still verified (disable.ts:40-45) before either branch. All codes are cleared on disable.
contracts.visible_effect: The DisableTwoFactorModal maps the new error codes to messages.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing encryption key throws, which surfaces as a 500 and the generic error in the modal.

summary: Backup codes as written are a password bypass. The login check for a backup code replaces TOTP verification. In the code before it, a non-empty totpCode already skips the password check. So a request carrying any totpCode and one valid backup code logs in with neither a password nor the authenticator. Also: codes are compared case-sensitively against lowercase hex, though the input suggests uppercase. Two concurrent logins can use the same code. Dismissing the enable dialog on the backup-codes step leaves the settings switch showing 2FA as off. The missing-codes message points to a settings option that does not exist.
